candidates.title: GEAR LOCK
candidates.description: Drag in an arc around a pivot to rotate a gear, releasing when its notch aligns with a shrinking-tolerance target angle.

candidates.title: COMET LEAD
candidates.description: Tap ahead along a comet's revealed path to place an interceptor where it will be, not where it currently is.

candidates.title: SLING NODES
candidates.description: Drag back and release to flick a puck with vector-based power at holes, managing which queued puck to launch next.

candidates.title: TRACE ROUTE
candidates.description: Drag one continuous stroke through numbered nodes in order without letting the line cross itself.

candidates.title: PULSE GATE
candidates.description: Tap whichever gate is currently 'hot' on a shared rotating beat, tracking both the target and the shared tempo.

candidates.title: MIRROR HOLD
candidates.description: Hold one of two zones to pull a shared marker toward it while the unheld zone's stamina regenerates, forcing alternation to hold a moving band.

candidates.title: CIRCUIT ECHO
candidates.description: Watch a growing sequence of flashed circuit nodes, then tap them back in the same order from memory.

candidates.title: DRIFT NET
candidates.description: Drag a sweeping net across the field to corral drifting orbs, where dragging faster covers more ground but narrows the capture width.

candidates.title: COLOR MIX TAP
candidates.description: Tap two differently-colored source orbs in sequence to blend a compound matching a shifting target hue.

candidates.title: BIN SORT MEMORY
candidates.description: Drag a stream of items into bins matching a mapping shown briefly at the round's start, then hidden.

candidates.title: TENSION LINE
candidates.description: Drag to stretch a line from a fixed anchor, releasing to commit before rising stretch distance triggers a snap-back.

candidates.title: PULSE SLICE
candidates.description: Drag one slicing stroke across a bundle of independently pulsing wires, scoring only the ones crossed during their lit phase.

reason: CIRCUIT ECHO scored highest overall and led on C2/C4/C5/C6 since its watch-then-reproduce memory loop is instantly graspable, its tap-only input is the most reliable to implement and verify, and every tap resolves with immediate visual/score feedback, while its hidden-order recall decision is genuinely distinct from the scan-and-order and discrimination mechanics already in the catalog.
